question: Bind — ATK, 8-1 up, 5v5, you hold an Operator scoped on an A Cubby angle while your team sets up the round. Nobody is peeking you yet. What is the disciplined Op play?

options.label: Hold the scoped angle patiently and only take the shot you are already set up for; re-position if it goes stale
options.explication_courte: Duel selection with an Op means taking ONLY the fights your crosshair is pre-set for. Holding the pre-aimed lane converts any peeker into a near-free pick, and if the angle dies you slip to a new one — you never gift the enemy a duel on their terms.

sources_option.citation: Only take the duels you are pre-aimed and positioned for; the Operator rewards the player who holds and refuses off-angle fights

options.label: Aggressively wide-swing the Op to hunt a pick and open the map early
options.explication_courte: Wide-swinging an Op throws away its entire strength — the slow scope-in leaves you cold on any angle you weren't already set for, and a wide-swing is exactly the fight riflers beat. Great picks come from holding, not chasing.

sources_option.citation: Wide-swinging with an Operator surrenders its holding advantage and hands riflers the reaction-time edge

options.label: Jiggle-peek the angle repeatedly to bait shots and gather info on who is watching
options.explication_courte: Jiggling for info is a fine tool, but doing it constantly with an Op wastes your held pre-aim and can walk you into a rifler's pre-fire. It gathers info at the cost of the very setup that makes your Op valuable.

sources_option.citation: Jiggle-peeks harvest info cheaply, but over-peeking an angle trades your positional advantage for exposure

options.label: Un-scope and rush forward to force close-range fights with your sidearm
options.explication_courte: Abandoning a strong Op perch to rush into pistol range on a gun round throws away your weapon advantage entirely and picks the worst possible duel for an Op holder. This is anti-duel-selection.

sources_option.citation: Forcing close-range fights with an Op holder discards the range advantage that defines the weapon's role

explication_longue: Duel selection is the quiet skill that separates ranks: choosing only the fights you are already set up to win and refusing the rest. Up 8-1 on Bind, holding an Operator scoped on an A Cubby angle with nobody peeking you, the disciplined play is simply to hold that pre-aimed lane patiently — take only the shot your crosshair is already placed for, and if the angle goes stale, slip quietly to a fresh one. That is exactly how an Op converts value: any peeker crossing your pre-aim is a near-free pick, and you never hand the enemy a duel on their terms. Wide-swinging the Op to hunt a pick is the costly error — the slow scope-in leaves you cold on anything you weren't set for, and a wide-swing is precisely the fight riflers beat on reaction time. Constant jiggle-peeking is a fine info tool but overused it wastes your held pre-aim and can walk you into a pre-fire; it buys information at the price of the setup that makes your Op strong. Un-scoping to rush into sidearm range is the outright faute — on a gun round you would be trading away your entire weapon advantage to pick the worst possible fight for an Op holder. When you are ahead and holding a strong angle, let the game come to you: hold the shot you're set for, refuse the rest.

sources.citation: Duel selection with the Operator: hold your pre-aimed angle, take only the fights you're set up for, reposition rather than over-peek
